display.purpose: Hero headline only, weight 600 (heavier than every other heading), italic emphasis word drops to 400 for print-style contrast.

headline.purpose: Section titles below each eyebrow label.

title.purpose: One shared size for every card/item title: services, value props, process steps, FAQ questions.

body.purpose: All readable paragraph copy, 16px minimum, capped near 38-65ch.

secondary.purpose: Supporting UI text: nav links, buttons, footer links, attribution. Never used for sentences meant to be read closely.

label.purpose: Uppercase kicker above every section heading, micro-labels, footer copyright.

shadows.name: card-hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Applied only on card :hover, paired with translateY(-6px). Never present at rest.

shadows.name: badge-resting
shadows.purpose: The two small badges overlapping the About photo (years-of-experience stat, pull quote).

shadows.name: floating-action
shadows.purpose: Fixed WhatsApp button; shadow tinted with the accent's own hue.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Scroll-reveal entrances and the mobile menu slide-in; an ease-out-quint feel, no bounce.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: Buttons and cards on hover: brightness/background shift plus a small translateY.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The booking/WhatsApp action. Solid red, sharp corners, brightens on hover rather than changing hue.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 13px 26px; font-family: 'Manrope', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.03em; background: #E53935; border: 1px solid #E53935; color: #fff; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 0.3s ease, transform 0.3s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(0.88); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #E53935; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary/tertiary action on a light surface. Transparent, fills solid black on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 13px 26px; font-family: 'Manrope', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.03em; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #333333; color: #333333; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.3s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #000000; border-color: #000000; color: #fff; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #333333; outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview: Mind & Soul reads like a well-set page in a printed magazine that happens to be about therapy, not like a wellness app or a Canva template with a leaf icon. The base is paper-white and three tiers of gray, set in a serif/sans pairing with generous whitespace and hairline rules instead of boxes and shadows. Red appears exactly where a decision needs to happen and nowhere else: it is punctuation, not paint. This system explicitly rejects the generic "therapist template" (leaf/hand icons, pastel gradients, stock-photo warmth) and the cold corporate-clinical look (navy, sterile grids, hospital whites). It also rejects decorating for its own sake: no drop shadows as default elevation, no rounded-everything softness, no gradient text, no card-in-a-card nesting.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-white and gray-scale carry over 90% of every screen; red is reserved for the single most important action or number in view.
Serif display type (Fraunces) for anything that should feel considered and human; sans (Manrope) for everything functional.
Flat surfaces, hairline dividers, sharp corners; the rare dark section exists for rhythm, not by default.
Mobile is the primary reading surface: long stacks become single-row, swipeable carousels rather than tall vertical stacks.

rules.name: The Rationed Red Rule
rules.body: Red never covers a surface larger than a button or a badge. If a whole section wants to feel important, it goes to Editorial Black or a mid-gray dark surface, not red.

rules.name: The Readable Gray Rule
rules.body: Quiet Gray (#9E9E9E) is for icons and truly decorative marks only. Anything a visitor is meant to read is Reading Ink (#333333) or darker.

rules.name: The Serif-Says-It-Matters Rule
rules.body: If a piece of text is switched into Fraunces italic, it is because that specific phrase or figure is the emotional or informational point of its section. Italic serif is never used decoratively.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing has a shadow until it does something (hover) or needs to read as a physical object overlapping a photo. A static card is always flat.

dos: Do keep the accent to Editorial Red (#E53935) and nothing else.
Do put anything meant to be read in Reading Ink (#333333) or Editorial Black, never in Quiet Gray (#9E9E9E).
Do use the shared-hairline-grid construction for new card rows instead of giving every card its own border and shadow.
Do convert long, repetitive mobile stacks into the horizontal scroll-snap carousel pattern rather than letting them stack vertically for multiple screens of scroll.
Do treat mobile as the primary surface and verify nothing overlaps the fixed header.
donts: Don't use the generic "therapist template" look: leaf/hand icons, pastel gradient washes, stock-photo-warm color grading.
Don't go cold-corporate/clinical: no navy-and-white hospital palette, no sterile grid layouts.
Don't add drop shadows to a card or button at rest.
Don't round corners, except the circular floating WhatsApp button and the circular practice logo mark.
Don't let red cover a background, a section, or more than a button/badge-sized area.
Don't fabricate content to fill a section: every fact on this page must come from the practitioner directly.
